lines.text: In December 1995, a real probe fell into Jupiter, and it kept talking for fifty-eight minutes.
In that time, it sent back data from a fall of one hundred fifty-six kilometres.
Sounds deep. But Jupiter's radius is more than seventy-one thousand kilometres.
So the probe covered less than a quarter of one percent of the way to the centre, by our sum.
Shrink that trip to a hundred metres, and the probe got about twenty-two centimetres.
Then the signal stopped, at twenty-three times the air pressure at Earth's surface. Nothing more was heard.
So what fills the rest of the way down, and is there anything at the bottom to land on?
The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
